_**Crazy Horse**_ is the debut album by [Crazy Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crazy_Horse_(band) "Crazy Horse (band)"), released in 1971 by [Reprise Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reprise_Records "Reprise Records"). It is the only album by the band to feature [Danny Whitten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Whitten "Danny Whitten") recorded without [Neil Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Young "Neil Young"), and it peaked at No. 84 on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") album chart.

## Background

Members of this band had already released an album in 1968 as The Rockets and had appeared on record twice with Neil Young as [Crazy Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crazy_Horse_(band) "Crazy Horse (band)"). The core trio from the Rockets, [Danny Whitten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Whitten "Danny Whitten"), [Billy Talbot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Talbot "Billy Talbot"), and [Ralph Molina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Molina "Ralph Molina"), provided instrumental backing for Young's 1969 album _[Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody_Knows_This_Is_Nowhere "Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere")_, and performed on most songs from Young's 1970 album _[After the Gold Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_the_Gold_Rush "After the Gold Rush")_. Producer/keyboardist [Jack Nitzsche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Nitzsche "Jack Nitzsche"), who had been a member of [Phil Spector's Wrecking Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wrecking_Crew_(music) "The Wrecking Crew (music)") and played on records by [the Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones"), had worked with Young on his [debut solo album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Young_(album) "Neil Young (album)") and on tracks for [Buffalo Springfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Springfield "Buffalo Springfield"). He was drafted into Crazy Horse to back up Young on their [short tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_at_the_Fillmore_East_(Neil_Young_album) "Live at the Fillmore East (Neil Young album)") in early 1970. During sessions for _Gold Rush_, they met teenage multi-instrumentalist [Nils Lofgren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nils_Lofgren "Nils Lofgren"), who joined the band in time for this album. The band got a contract with [Reprise Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reprise_Records "Reprise Records") after the exposure garnered from their association with Young.

This was Whitten's last recording before his dismissal from the group and subsequent death from an [alcohol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcohol_(drug) "Alcohol (drug)")/ [diazepam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diazepam "Diazepam") overdose in 1972. Due to Whitten’s increasingly erratic performances (stemming from a [heroin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroin "Heroin") addiction and longstanding [rheumatoid arthritis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rheumatoid_arthritis "Rheumatoid arthritis")), guitarist [Ry Cooder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ry_Cooder "Ry Cooder") was retained as a [session musician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Session_musician "Session musician") on three tracks. Cooder had worked previously with Nitzsche on sessions for the Stones and Young's debut solo album.

The album contains compositions from four principal writers. Whitten's ballad " [I Don't Want to Talk About It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don't_Want_to_Talk_About_It "I Don't Want to Talk About It")" would be covered by a variety of artists, including [Rita Coolidge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Coolidge "Rita Coolidge"); [Everything but the Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everything_but_the_Girl "Everything but the Girl") on their 1988 album _[Idlewild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idlewild_(Everything_but_the_Girl_album) "Idlewild (Everything but the Girl album)")_; and [Rod Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_Stewart "Rod Stewart"), who had a chart-topping hit with the song in the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), taken from his 1975 album _[Atlantic Crossing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Crossing "Atlantic Crossing")_. Young's "Dance Dance Dance" was covered by [The New Seekers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Seekers "The New Seekers") in 1972, and [Randy Newman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Newman "Randy Newman") had already performed Nitzsche's "Gone Dead Train" on the soundtrack for the 1970 film _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance_(film) "Performance (film)")_ by [Donald Cammell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Cammell "Donald Cammell") and [Nicolas Roeg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Roeg "Nicolas Roeg"). The song was also covered by the Scottish hard rock band [Nazareth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazareth_(band) "Nazareth (band)") on their 1977 album _[Expect No Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expect_No_Mercy "Expect No Mercy")_;[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crazy_Horse_(album)#cite_note-4) the group had previously covered "Beggars Day" on their 1975 album _[Hair of the Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_of_the_Dog_(album) "Hair of the Dog (album)")_.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crazy_Horse_(album)#cite_note-5)

A live version of "Downtown" by Whitten and Young would appear on Young's 1975 album _[Tonight's the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonight's_the_Night_(Neil_Young_album) "Tonight's the Night (Neil Young album)")_, entitled "(Come On Baby Let's Go) Downtown." On this Crazy Horse album and Neil Young's 2006 archival release _[Live at the Fillmore East 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_at_the_Fillmore_East_(Neil_Young_album) "Live at the Fillmore East (Neil Young album)")_, the song is credited to Whitten alone. This song is not to be confused with " [Downtown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_(Neil_Young_song) "Downtown (Neil Young song)")" from Young's 1995 album _[Mirror Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirror_Ball_(Neil_Young_album) "Mirror Ball (Neil Young album)")_.

_Crazy Horse_ was released on compact disc on March 22, 1994, as part of the [Warner Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Records "Warner Bros. Records") archive series, produced for compact disc by Lee Herschberg. It appeared in its entirety as part of [Rhino Handmade's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhino_Records "Rhino Records") _[Scratchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scratchy:_The_Complete_Reprise_Recordings "Scratchy: The Complete Reprise Recordings")_ compilation from 2005, which also included outtakes from the sessions for this album. The compilation is no longer in print.

## Personnel

- [Danny Whitten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Whitten "Danny Whitten") – [guitars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitars "Guitars"), [backing vocals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backing_vocals "Backing vocals"); [lead vocals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_vocals "Lead vocals") except as indicated below
- [Nils Lofgren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nils_Lofgren "Nils Lofgren") – guitars, backing vocals; lead vocals on "Beggar's Day"
- [Jack Nitzsche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Nitzsche "Jack Nitzsche") – [piano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano "Piano"), backing vocals; lead vocals on "Crow Jane Lady"
- [Billy Talbot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Talbot "Billy Talbot") – [bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_guitar "Bass guitar"), backing vocals
- [Ralph Molina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Molina "Ralph Molina") – [drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_kit "Drum kit"), backing vocals; lead vocals on "Dance, Dance, Dance"

Additional personnel

- [Ry Cooder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ry_Cooder "Ry Cooder") – [slide guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slide_guitar "Slide guitar") on "I Don't Want to Talk About It," "Dirty, Dirty" and "Crow Jane Lady"
- [Gib Guilbeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gib_Guilbeau "Gib Guilbeau") – [violin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violin "Violin") on "Dance, Dance, Dance"

- [Gary Burden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Burden "Gary Burden") – art direction, design

- [Lee Herschberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Herschberg?action=edit&redlink=1 "Lee Herschberg") – [digital mastering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mastering "Audio mastering")
